names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 15 iulie, «Sfinții Mucenici Chiric și Iulita», with the rank words left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 15 Ιουλίου, «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του», with the rank word and the kinship clause left off. The page's summary verse spells it «Ἰουλίττα» and «Ἰουλίτταν»; its first narrative sentence writes «Η Αγία Ιουλίτα» with one tau.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 15. јул ст. ст., „Св. муч. Кирик и Јулита.“ — „Св. муч.“ is the rank and the second of the two bare forenames the heading enumerates is the whole of the form; «mother of Cyricus» in the display name is the corpus’s own. `foldchk.py` returns no holder and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder — **and `julitta-of-caesarea` is a folder of this corpus whom this very book keeps sixteen days later, on the Julian 31 July**, so the two Julitta folders will fold with each other before this range is done. That is a prediction made here and answered there.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 15 iulie — «Sfinții Mucenici Chiric și Iulita»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 15ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 15 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and pairs mother and son exactly as the Romanian line does. The woman is the folder's own: Julitta of Iconium, mother of Cyricus, tortured before her child and dying shortly after him. The Greek page adds Iconium, the flight to Seleucia and Tarsus, the governor Alexander, and a long list of her relics — a forearm with flesh at the monastery of Pantokrator on Athos, portions at the Great Lavra, at Palaiokastritsa on Corfu and at Kykkos on Cyprus. No year is printed; the only mark of time is «έζησε κατά την εποχή του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού», the reign undated, so nothing is proposed for `dates`. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints one apolytikion, which names both mother and son, and it is taken onto both folders.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.07.2026 (15. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Кирик и Јулита.“

attestations.note: The second half of the day’s first entry; the same heading, quoted whole, stands over both rows, which is what §4 requires of an enumerated company — **and this entry is in fact hers**, the body opening „Ова светитељка беше од рода племићског“, this saint was of a noble family, and following her from her widowhood to her beheading. **`dates` WRITTEN WHERE THE FOLDER HAD NONE.** `dates: null` before. The Охридски пролог for 15. јул ст. ст. closes the passion „После многих мука и Јулита би мачем посечена, 304. год.“ — after many torments Julitta too was beheaded with the sword, in 304. The year closes the one scene, and „и Јулита“, Julitta too, is what makes it the year of both: the child suffered first and in the same trial, „Видећи како Кирик пострада пре ње“. Neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave a year. So `death` is 304 to 304, display «304», basis traditional, as on her son’s. The year stands on **her** beheading in the book’s own sentence, which is why it is written on both and not on him alone. `types` UNTOUCHED at `martyr`. **`widow` is not a word this vocabulary has** and nothing is written off „Рано обудове“, she was early widowed. No `office`, no `locations`. **WHAT IS NEW IS HER WHOLE COURSE.** Of a noble family; early widowed and left with a newborn child; living in the city of Iconium in Lycaonia and wholly given to the faith of Christ; she baptised her little son at once at his birth, and when he was three years old taught him the faith and prayer as much as a child of that age could receive. When Diocletian ordered the persecution of Christians and much innocent blood was shed in Iconium, she took her son and withdrew from the pagan wrath to the city of Seleucia — **„Но и тамо не беше боље“**, but there it was no better — and she was seized there and brought before the judge as a Christian. Having bravely declared her faith in the Lord Jesus, she saw the judge take her child on his knees to shake her; and after her son had been killed before her eyes she **gave thanks to God** that He had counted him worthy of a martyr’s crown, and after many torments was beheaded with the sword. **NO NEW `related` ROWS**, and the dedication at Ohrid is a dedication. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Chiric și Iulita, mama lui», Glasul 4 — the common of martyrs, printed there under the two names; the spelling «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own.

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest won from You, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Your strength they overthrew their tormentors and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At their prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ἡ καλλιμάρτυς τοῦ Χρίστου Ἰουλίττα, σὺν τριετεῖ ἀμνῶ αὐτῆς τῷ Κηρύκῳ, δικαστοὺ πρὸ βήματος παρέστησαν φαιδρῶς, εὔτολμοι κηρύττοντες. τὴν χριστώνυμον κλῆσιν, ἄμφω μὴ πτοούμενοι, ἀπειλᾶς τῶν τυρράνων καὶ στεφηφόροι νῦν ἐν οὐρανοίς, ἀγαλλιώνται. Χριστῷ παριστάμενοι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ', Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς ἐν τῷ Σταυρῷ — the only hymn on the page of «Άγιοι Κήρυκος και Ιουλίττα η μητέρα του», and it names both of them

english.text: Julitta, the fair martyr of Christ, together with Cyricus her three-year-old lamb, stood brightly before the judge's seat, preaching with courage the name of Christians; neither of them was dismayed at the threats of the tyrants, and now, crowned, they rejoice in the heavens, standing before Christ.

The year closes the one scene, and „и Јулита“, Julitta too, is what makes it the year of both: the child suffered first and in the same trial, „Видећи како Кирик пострада пре ње“.
